en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for its nearly perfect natural conical shape.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers.
Lake Taal in Batangas province is a freshwater lake located inside the main crater of Taal Volcano.
Luzon is the largest island in the Philippine archipelago, covering a land area of over 109,000 square kilometers.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered bird of prey endemic to the tropical forests of Mindanao.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered hills that turn brown during summer.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected marine sanctuary located in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
Mount Pinatubo in Zambales erupted violently in 1991, creating one of the largest volcanic calderas in the world.
The Philippines possesses some of the world's largest nickel reserves, which are primarily mined in Surigao and Palawan.
